demand-curve.svg: Demand curve labelled D for q equals 100 minus 2p: a downward-sloping straight line on axes with price p across and quantity q up, running from q equals 100 at a price of zero down to zero quantity at a price of 50
supply-curve.svg: Supply curve labelled S for q equals 20 plus 3p: an upward-sloping straight line on axes with price p across and quantity q up, starting at q equals 20 when the price is zero
market-equilibrium.svg: Demand curve D and supply curve S drawn on the same price-quantity axes, crossing at the equilibrium price p star of 16 and quantity q star of 68, marked by dashed lines to each axis
vector-geometric.svg: Vector v one drawn as a maroon arrow from the origin to the point (2, 1), with dashed guides marking 2 on the x-axis and 1 on the y-axis
vector-addition.svg: Vector addition by the parallelogram rule: arrows u from the origin to (9, 2) and v from the origin to (2, 5), dashed lines completing the parallelogram, and a maroon arrow labelled u plus v reaching its far corner, the sum at (11, 7)
linear-dependent.svg: Two linearly dependent vectors: a maroon arrow v one to (2, 4) and an ink arrow v two to (1, 2), lying along the same line through the origin
linear-independent.svg: Two linearly independent vectors: a maroon arrow v one to (1, 3) and an ink arrow v two to (3, 1), pointing in different directions from the origin
determinant-area.svg: Geometric interpretation of a determinant: arrows from the origin to (1, 3) and (2, 4), the columns of A, with dashed lines completing a shaded parallelogram whose area equals the absolute value of the determinant of A
ai-linal.jpeg: Four-panel comic: a person asks A.I. why it always wears a mask; the mask is lifted to reveal a matrix of entries a-one-one through a-m-n underneath, and the person says “let’s keep this on” - a joke that machine learning is linear algebra underneath
network-example.png: A directed network with three nodes: an arrow from node 1 to node 2, an arrow from node 2 to node 3, and an arrow from node 3 back to node 1
stem-linal.png: Comic showing a precarious tower of blocks labeled 'All of STEM' balancing on one small block labeled 'That one linear algebra course'
grades-production.svg: An upward-sloping curve for y equals x squared plus 20, on axes with hours studied across and grades up, rising from 20 at zero hours to 120 at ten hours and getting steeper as hours increase
grades-tangent.svg: The same curve for y equals x squared plus 20, with a dashed straight line touching it at the point where x is 6 and y is 56; the tangent line has slope 12, which is f prime of 6
limit-jump.svg: A curve in two pieces with a gap at x equals zero: the left piece rises and stops just below the value 5, and the right piece starts just above the value 7 and keeps rising, with open circles at both ends showing the function jumps from 5 to 7
limit-abs.svg: The graph of f of x equals four x minus four over the absolute value of x minus one: a horizontal line at negative 4 for x less than 1 and a horizontal line at positive 4 for x greater than 1, with open circles at x equals 1 on both
discontinuity.svg: The line y equals 2x plus 1 drawn from x equals negative 1 to x equals 2, with an open circle at the point (1, 3) where the line has a hole, and a filled dot below it at (1, 2) showing the value of the function at x equals 1
abs-value.svg: A V-shaped graph of y equals the absolute value of x for x from negative 4 to 4: a straight line falling to a sharp corner at the origin and rising again, with no break anywhere
inverse-mirror.svg: Three lines on the same axes, each running from negative 25 to 25: the steep line y equals 7x plus 21, the flat line y equals x minus 21 over 7, and a dashed 45-degree line y equals x between them; the two solid lines are reflections of each other across the dashed line
exp-function.svg: Graph of y equals e to the x for x from negative 2 to 2: a curve that stays just above the x-axis on the left, passes through the point (0, 1), and rises ever more steeply to about 7.4 at x equals 2
log-function.svg: Graph of y equals the natural log of x for x from just above 0 to 8: a curve that rises steeply from far below the x-axis near x equals 0, crosses the x-axis at the point (1, 0), and keeps rising ever more slowly to about 2.1 at x equals 8
partial-derivative.svg: A dome-shaped surface z equals f of x and y over x and y from negative 2 to 2. A maroon curve runs along the surface where y is held fixed at b, labeled graph of f of x and b. A dark dot marks the point (a, b, f(a, b)) on that curve, and a straight line touches the curve at the dot, labeled tangent line, slope partial f over partial x at (a, b)
area-rectangles.svg: A concave curve f of x over the interval from x zero to x five, with five grey rectangles of equal width standing under it, each as tall as the curve at its left edge; the fourth rectangle's width is marked delta x three and its height f of x three
area-fine.svg: The same concave curve with twenty narrow grey rectangles under it, which together fill the region under the curve almost exactly
consumer-surplus.svg: The demand curve p equals 48 minus Q squared, falling from a price of 48 at zero quantity and getting steeper as quantity rises, with dashed lines marking the market price of 12 on the price axis and the quantity of 6 on the quantity axis, meeting at a point on the curve
discont-jump.svg: A line of slope 1 rising to an open circle at the point (1, 2), then jumping up to a filled dot at (1, 3) and continuing with slope 1 from there
discont-hole.svg: A line of slope 1 with a hole, an open circle, at the point (1, 2), and an isolated filled dot above the hole at (1, 3); the line continues past the hole with the same slope
market-nonlinear.svg: Price on the vertical axis and quantity on the horizontal axis; a maroon downward-sloping demand curve D and a grey upward-sloping supply curve S cross at a point marked with dashed lines to P star on the price axis and Q star on the quantity axis
global-vs-local.svg: A wavy curve f of x with several peaks and troughs. The highest peak is marked global max and the lowest trough global min; the other peaks are marked local max and the other troughs local min
inflection.svg: The S-shaped curve y equals x cubed, rising through the origin where it flattens out momentarily. A dot marks the origin with the note f prime of 0 equals 0 but no extremum
first-derivative-test.svg: A curve that rises, peaks where a dashed horizontal tangent is drawn and labeled f prime of x equals 0, falls to a trough with another dashed horizontal tangent labeled the same way, then rises again. The rising stretches are labeled f prime of x greater than 0 and the falling stretch f prime of x less than 0
ac-mc.svg: A clearly U-shaped average cost curve AC in maroon that falls steeply, bottoms out, and rises again, and a marginal cost curve MC in grey that dips and then rises steeply, crossing AC exactly at AC's lowest point. A dot and a dashed vertical line mark that point at the quantity Q star
quartic.svg: The graph of y equals x to the fourth power: a flat-bottomed U shape with its minimum at the origin, where a dot is drawn
concave-chord.svg: A concave curve rising and flattening, with two points on it at x one and x two joined by a dashed chord. At the midpoint x m between them, the point on the curve, labeled f of x m, sits above the point on the chord
convex-chord.svg: A convex curve rising ever more steeply, with two points on it at x one and x two joined by a dashed chord. At the midpoint x m between them, the point on the curve, labeled f of x m, sits below the point on the chord
cubic.svg: The graph of y equals x cubed, drawn solid for x at least 0 where it bends upward, and dashed for negative x where it bends downward, passing through the origin
quad-min.svg: The upward-opening parabola y equals 3 x squared plus 3, symmetric about the vertical axis, with a dot at its lowest point (0, 3)
cubic-hw.svg: The curve y equals x cubed minus 3 x plus 5, drawn solid for x at least 0 and dashed for negative x. Dots mark the local minimum at (1, 3) on the solid part and the local maximum at (negative 1, 7) on the dashed part
x-plus-recip.svg: The two branches of y equals x plus 1 over x. The right branch, for positive x, has a dot at its lowest point (1, 2); the left branch, for negative x, has a dot at its highest point (negative 1, negative 2), which lies below the minimum of the right branch
concave-examples.svg: Two panels. Panel a: a curve that rises like a square root and then continues as a flat horizontal line, so it is concave but contains a straight segment. Panel b: a straight line through the origin with slope 1, which is both concave and convex
stationary-points.svg: A dashed horizontal line f of x equals 1 and a maroon parabola g of x with its minimum at (3, 1), marked by a dot, touching the line there
